subject: GridPay discovery — ops intake + capacity deep-dive next steps
messages:
From: Andrew Lowe <andrew.lowe@gridpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick post-call recap + request to schedule capacity deep-dive

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful walkthrough. A few quick notes from our side after the discovery call: 

- Primary workload: fraud scoring + transaction description enrichment (batch + sync API).
- Peak traffic: ~650 req/s during morning clearing window (10–11am PT), median 220 req/s.
- Typical prompt lengths: 150–400 tokens; occasional large batches with 1k token context for historical lookups.
- Latency constraints: 95th percentile < 220ms for sync paths; batch can tolerate several seconds.

We want to move to a dedicated-capacity sizing discussion to confirm GPU footprint and autoscale policy. Can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week? Diego (their infra lead) will want to go through KV cache behavior and batching tradeoffs. We can share a small sample of traffic/exported logs if that helps — attaching a CSV sample.

Proposed windows (PT):
- Tue 27 Apr: 09:00–11:00 or 15:00–17:00
- Wed 28 Apr: 10:00–12:00

If those don't work, happy to send a Calendly link.

Attachments: gridpay_traffic_sample.csv (sample 2 hours of request logs)

Thanks,
Andrew Lowe
Director of Engineering, GridPay
andre.w.lowe@gridpay.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Lowe <andrew.lowe@gridpay.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + request to schedule capacity deep-dive

Thanks Andrew — great notes and appreciate the sample. Diego and Karthik are copied; they'll drive the sizing conversation. 

Short reply with next steps: 
1) We'll review the CSV and prepare an initial sizing hypothesis (GPU count, preferred instance family, KV cache sizing) ahead of the call.
2) Please complete the attached intake worksheet so we can validate peak sequence lengths, encoding, and any async batch SLAs (worksheet attached: redwood_dedicated_intake.xlsx).
3) Proposed time: Wed 28 Apr 10:00–11:00 PT — we'll block this tentatively; if you prefer Tue 27 at 15:00 PT we can switch.

Diego — can you confirm you can cover KV/cache behavior and batching patterns? Karthik — please prepare notes on quantization/throughput tradeoffs and a quick list of metrics we'll ask them to provide (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, average batch size).

If that works Andrew, confirm and we'll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Lowe <andrew.lowe@gridpay.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + request to schedule capacity deep-dive

On Mon, 26 Apr 2027 at 08:17 -0700, Diego Fernandez wrote:
> Hi team — looping in some specific asks so we can make the deep-dive productive.
> 
> 1) Can you add a small sample of request/response size distribution (CSV is fine). We need token counts per request and whether requests include long historical context.
> 2) Do you expect traffic bursts to be single-region or multi-region? If multi-region, what % to each region?
> 3) Any strict data residency or on-prem constraints for the model outputs?
> 
> I'll prepare a short runbook of what we'll cover: kernel selection, batch sizing + headroom, prefix/KV cache configuration, and cost tradeoffs for quantized vs fp16 variants.

I can lead the KV/cache section and demo results from a similar payment workload. Also happy to take the first 15 minutes for a quick architecture alignment so we understand where caching fits (gateway vs service-level).

Diego
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
From: Andrew Lowe <andrew.lowe@gridpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + request to schedule capacity deep-dive

Evelyn, Diego — thanks. I've attached an expanded sample that includes token counts and a short note about regional distribution. A couple clarifications: 

- Bursts are primarily US-west (90%), fallback to US-east for redundancy (10%).
- Historical context is included for ~8% of requests; those average 900–1,100 tokens.
- There is no on-prem constraint at this stage; we prefer a VPC private deployment but can use hosted dedicated.

I can do Wed 28 Apr 10:00–11:00 PT. Please send an invite. Attachment: gridpay_traffic_sample.csv (expanded, includes tokens column).

—Andrew
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Lowe <andrew.lowe@gridpay.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + request to schedule capacity deep-dive

Perfect — invite sent. Agenda (in the calendar description):
- 10:00–10:15: Architecture & traffic profile confirmation (Evelyn)
- 10:15–10:35: KV cache and batching patterns (Diego)
- 10:35–10:50: Model selection, quantization, and throughput estimates (Karthik)
- 10:50–11:00: Action items, follow-ups, and next steps (all)

Please review the intake worksheet before the call and if possible add a small section with expected p50/p95 numbers and a couple of Postman examples for sync endpoints. Looking forward to it.

Calendar link: https://calendly.com/redwood-eval/deep-dive-60
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/GP-2027-051

Evelyn
